reconstructed_theorem_text: Let S = Bool × Bool be the discrete four-state space, write δ_z for the point mass at z, and let ¬b denote Boolean negation. Define π = (3/8)δ_(false,false) + (1/8)δ_(false,true) + (1/8)δ_(true,false) + (3/8)δ_(true,true). For x = (x₁,x₂) in S, define kernels P and Q by P(x,·) = (3/4)δ_(x₂,x₂) + (1/4)δ_(¬x₂,x₂) and Q(x,·) = (3/4)δ_(x₁,x₁) + (1/4)δ_(x₁,¬x₁). The displayed weights and singleton evaluations are extended nonnegative reals. Then π is a probability measure and π({x}) > 0 for every x in S; P and Q are Markov kernels; for every b in Bool, π({z in S : z₂ = b}) = 1/2 and π({z in S : z₁ = b}) = 1/2; for every x,y in S, P(x,{y}) is 2·π({y}) if y₂ = x₂ and 0 otherwise; for every x,y in S, Q(x,{y}) is 2·π({y}) if y₁ = x₁ and 0 otherwise; P and Q are each reversible with respect to π; and Q ∘ P, the kernel obtained by applying P first and Q second, leaves π invariant but is not reversible with respect to π.
objects: S is the discrete four-state space Bool × Bool. The fixed measure π assigns masses 3/8, 1/8, 1/8, 3/8 to (false,false), (false,true), (true,false), (true,true), respectively. For x=(x₁,x₂), the row of P has point masses 3/4 at (x₂,x₂) and 1/4 at (¬x₂,x₂), while the row of Q has point masses 3/4 at (x₁,x₁) and 1/4 at (x₁,¬x₁). The composite kernel is Q ∘ P.
domains: All states x, y, z are in Bool × Bool with its discrete measurable structure; b and each coordinate are in Bool. Point masses are measures on that space; P and Q have that space as both source and target. Displayed weights and singleton evaluations are extended nonnegative reals.
quantifiers: The theorem has no outer parameter quantification or existential choice. In the conjunction, positivity holds for every x in Bool × Bool; both marginal equalities hold for every b in Bool; the P-row formula and the Q-row formula each hold for every x,y in Bool × Bool. The z in each marginal set is bound by that set comprehension.
assumptions: No premises. The three local have binders fix π, P and Q by definition. Probability, strict singleton positivity, and the Markov-kernel properties are conclusions, not assumptions.
conclusion: The conjunction asserts that π is a probability measure, π({x}) > 0 for every state x, and P and Q are Markov kernels. For every Boolean b, π({z : z₂=b}) = 1/2 and π({z : z₁=b}) = 1/2. For all states x,y, P(x,{y}) = 2·π({y}) when y₂=x₂ and 0 otherwise; for all states x,y, Q(x,{y}) = 2·π({y}) when y₁=x₁ and 0 otherwise. P and Q are each reversible with respect to π. Q ∘ P is invariant with respect to π and is not reversible with respect to π.
scopes: All assertions share the three fixed local definitions and are joined by conjunction. Each row formula has its own universal state-pair scope and its own conditional on coordinate equality. The two marginal equalities lie together under the same Boolean quantifier. The final negation applies only to reversibility of Q ∘ P with respect to π, not to its invariance or to reversibility of P or Q. Composition applies P first and Q second.
constant_dependencies: π depends only on the fixed Boolean point masses and fixed weights 3/8 and 1/8. The row definitions of P and Q use point masses, Boolean negation, and fixed weights 3/4 and 1/4; P's row depends only on the input's second coordinate and Q's only on its first, and neither definition uses π. The marginal value 1/2 and row multiplier 2 are fixed. Reversibility uses equality of the stationary set fluxes for the specified kernel and π; invariance uses the pushforward of π along the specified kernel. No constant depends on any free parameter.
